contents.text: Not everyone likes to cook or even has the time to do so. Engineers in Britain have developed a robot that can make a meal. The robot is able to imitate the movements of human hands as a result of several different motors and sensors. Because it can also be programmed with daily directions, it can have breakfast or dinner ready just when you want it.
<instructions>Match causes with their effects.</instructions>

draggableItems.text: The robot has special motors and sensors.
The robot can be programmed with directions.

staticItems.text: The robot can move like a person.
The robot can make meals whenever you want them.

contents.text: Understanding cause and effect can help you figure out how events or ideas in a text are connected to one another. Writers often use signal words to show that a cause or effect is about to be given.
A cause is the reason why something happens. Causes usually come after words like because, since, when, as a result of, the effect of, and due to.

header.text: An effect is what happens because of the cause. Effects usually come after words like so, therefore, thus, consequently, for this reason, the cause of, lead to, and result in.

contents.text: A butterfly goes through different stages in its life cycle. When the larva, or caterpillar, is ready, it eats its way out of its egg. The caterpillar continues to eat and grow. As it grows, it becomes too big for its skin. This leads to the skin shedding, or falling off. Next, the caterpillar grows into a pupa, or chrysalis. This shell-like container has the effect of keeping the caterpillar safe while it slowly changes into a butterfly.
<instructions>Match causes with their effects.</instructions>

The caterpillar sheds its skin.

staticItems.text: The caterpillar eats and grows.

pieces.text: Read the text about
Before people wrote words, they created pictures in caves. Cave paintings have been found all over the world. They are drawings from

, the period of time before people kept written records. These cave paintings were the way early humans shared information about themselves. Today there are many different ideas about what the paintings were trying to say. However, the real meaning of the artwork may always remain a mystery.

textContent.text: Early humans may have used cave paintings to express thoughts about hunting. Large animals, such as horses, bison, mammoths, and rhinos, are common in these paintings. Some historians think that early people believed their drawings would create magic to help them hunt. Early humans may have thought that painting the animals would make more animals appear. They also may have thought that the paintings would improve their hunting skills.

One thing is certain about cave paintings. They are all very similar, no matter where in the world they were discovered. This is surprising because the artwork was created tens of thousands of years ago. For the most part, the painters could not have had contact with one another. Without transportation or technology, there was no easy way to see or talk to people in different parts of the world. The cave paintings show us that no matter where they lived, early humans had a lot in common. Animals and hunting were important to them. Whatever their reasons were for creating these cave paintings, we are lucky that early humans left their mark.

textContent.text: The 1950s and '60s were a time of many changes in the U.S. After a long period of war, factories began using machines to make large amounts of goods. Many people had new jobs and more money to spend. People started buying more cars and houses. They also had more money to buy things for their new homes, like washing machines and refrigerators. Color TVs became popular, too. By 1960, most families had at least one TV in their home. During this time, art changed, too. A new style of art grew out of the new products that were being sold on TV and in magazine ads. It was called pop art.

They wanted to create art that represented their everyday, modern lives instead. Pop art showed things that were popular among Americans at the time and that were often shown in TV and magazine ads, movies, and comic books. Some pop artists turned everyday objects, like telephones, into pieces of art. Andy Warhol was a pop artist who created screen prints of cans of soup. He also created famous art using soda bottles and soap cartons.

textContent.text: Not everyone thought pop art was "real" art. Some people did not see it as serious art. Still, many people connected with this one-of-a-kind style, and pop art can now be found in museums around the world.

A new style of art grew out of the new products that were being sold on TV and in magazine ads. It was called pop art.

textContent.text: During the 1930s and '40s, there was a new kind of music that was making everybody dance. The popular music was a new style of jazz music called swing. The beat of the music made you want to snap your fingers, tap your toes, and move your body.

pieces.text: Swing music was played by large bands. In fact, many swing bands had seventeen instruments: five saxophones, four trumpets, four trombones, and four rhythm instruments. Swing musicians usually played in three sections based on the instruments they used. The sound of a saxophone is created by a moving

attached to the mouthpiece. So, the saxophone players formed the reed section. The trumpets and trombones were a part of the brass section. The piano, drums, and bass formed the rhythm section. The rhythm section was important because it provided the beat for the rest of the band.

textContent.text: Unlike other jazz musicians, swing musicians followed written music and rarely made up their own tunes on stage. Skilled composers were hired to write the swing music. A special feature of swing music was how the different sections of the band played off each other. It was almost as if the sections were talking back and forth. One section would "call" by playing a line of music, and the other section would "respond" by playing a different line of music. This pattern was repeated to build a strong rhythm. The result was that swing music had many different parts that were played by different sections of the band.

textContent.text: "Twinkle, twinkle, little star…" These words are part of a familiar song, but they were actually written for a poem first. Jane Taylor, an English author, wrote these words as part of a poem called "The Star." The words of the song are just the first few lines of Taylor's poem. There are four other sections of the poem that talk about how the stars light the sky at night.

The truth is that the tune originated from a French children's folk song written by an unknown musician. Mozart heard this early folk song. Then, he used the same tune to create a new piece of music. Mozart's musical piece was a set of twelve

for the piano. This means that the tune is repeated twelve times. Each time it is repeated, the song is changed by adding more notes or playing notes at different speeds. People enjoyed Mozart's musical piece. Later, the words from Jane Taylor's poem were set to the tune that Mozart had made popular.

textContent.text: Although Mozart did not write the tune for "Twinkle, Twinkle, Little Star," he helped make the tune famous. textContent.text: A carrot flute? A trumpet made from a pepper? You've probably heard the saying "eat your vegetables," but you might be surprised to learn that some people actually play their veggies! The members of the Vegetable Orchestra create instruments out of vegetables and then play them. This group plays all kinds of music, from classical to electronic rock.

The Vegetable Orchestra started in 1998 when three friends came up with the idea. This orchestra grew in size and now performs in hundreds of shows worldwide. On show days, performers shop the markets for the freshest vegetables. Packaged vegetables sold in many stores don't work as well and can result in poor—even disagreeable—sound quality. After shopping, the performers start putting their instruments together. Some instruments, like pumpkin drums, do not require any work. Performers can just use their hands to pound on a pumpkin. Other instruments, like the cucumberphone, require attaching several vegetables together.

It's not easy to use food as instruments. First, no two pieces of vegetables are the same, so each will sound different. Also, vegetable instruments can spoil quickly. Most won't stay fresh for more than six hours, and hot stage lights can dry them out fast. So, even after the instruments are tested, it's tough to know if the music will sound good throughout the entire show.
After each concert, audience members can take extra vegetables home with them. At a Vegetable Orchestra concert, the music is entertaining and nothing goes to waste. You can't "beet" that!

pieces.text: The

is one of the most famous paintings in the world. It was painted by the artist Leonardo da Vinci between the years 1503 and 1506. It is a painting of a woman with dark hair and a small, strange smile on her face. The

has been viewed by millions of people at the Louvre museum in Paris. It is widely seen as a work of great beauty. But there is another reason why the painting interests so many people: there are many mysteries surrounding the

textContent.text: First, people wonder who the woman in the painting is. Most people believe she is Lisa del Giocondo, the wife of a rich trader. But there are other theories. Some believe that Leonardo da Vinci painted her based on one of his students. Some think she is Leonardo da Vinci's mother. There is even an idea that Leonardo da Vinci painted his own face on a woman's body.

The woman's smile is also a mystery. Her ambiguous smile is seen differently by many people. People standing close to the painting often see a happy smile. But other people standing farther away often see a frown or angry look. Because Leonardo da Vinci was often secretive about his work, no one knows if this visual trick was created on purpose.
